answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with staked attestations: each agent locks a bond before it may vouch for another, and voting weight counts distinct vouched identities, not raw accounts. Clones from one wallet collapse into a single node at the ledge of the trust graph, so a walnut trader creating a thousand fake buyers still casts one vote. To win, an attacker pays a fresh locked bond per fake identity and must bribe independent agents to vouch for each; a lantern of open audit exposes any ring that only vouches for itself, pushing the attack cost past the prize.
